To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a micromachining process has been developed and used for fabricating a 2DOF MEMS stage.
the proposed 2DOF MEMS stage can achieve a dynamic range of 13.31 µm and a positioning accuracy of 2.2 nm.
a 2DOF micro-stage has been designed, fabricated and tested with a capacitive readout system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a MEMS-based 2DOF nanostage that can be used in a variety of micro- and nanomanipulation applications.
the development of a micromechanical 2DOF stage for nanoscale manipulation.
the design of an electrostatically actuated MEMS 2DOF stage with capacitive sensing capability, and the fabrication of a prototype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design and fabrication process of this MEMS stage is a success.
the proposed 2DOF stage is a promising solution for the applications requiring high positioning precision and large dynamic range.
the design, fabrication, characterization, and testing of a micromechanical two degree of freedom nanopositioner has been presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design and fabrication of the 2DOF MEMS stage is completed and the stage can be used as a nanopositioner in the micro/nanomanufacturing processes.
we have designed and tested a micromachining-based 2DOF microstage with integrated capacitive sensors.
the 2DOF microstage is capable of providing a large displacement range with a high resolution, which can be useful in applications such as optical scanning, microassembly and micro-manipulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design a 2DOF MEMS stage with integrated displacement sensors, and the capacitive sensing circuit can be implemented with a commercially available readout IC.
the capacitive sensing can be used in conjunction with the actuation to improve the performance of the microstage.
the design of the 2DOF MEMS nanopositioner is a good starting point for future work in the design of MEMS stages with more degrees of freedom.
